  • Pledge of Support: When the Prophet inquired whether his own tribe would expel him, Waraqah affirmed that no messenger brought what he brought without facing hostility, pledging his staunch support if he lived to that day.

Passing & Historical Legacy

Waraqah passed away shortly thereafter during the period of cessation of revelation (Fatra). In authenticated narrations (Sahih Muslim and Sunan al-Tirmidhi), the Prophet ﷺ confirmed that he saw Waraqah in a dream clothed in white or walking in gardens of Paradise due to his early affirmation of truth.

Abu Bakar Asshiddiq.meta:
Birth name: Abdullah bin Abi Quhafah
Title: Ash-Shiddiq, Al-Atiq
Era/Setting: Mecca and Medina, 7th century CE
Abu Bakar Asshiddiq.body:
Lineage & Early Life

Abdullah bin Abi Quhafah (Abu Bakar Asshiddiq) hailed from the Banu Taym clan of Quraysh. Renowned throughout Mecca for his noble lineage, encyclopedic knowledge of Arab genealogy, immaculate morals, and successful commercial trading, he abstained from alcohol and pagan worship even in the pre-Islamic era.

Key Events & Historical Role

1. First Adult Male to Accept Islam

  • Unhesitating Faith: As the intimate childhood friend of Muhammad ﷺ, Abu Bakar accepted Islam immediately without a trace of hesitation when invited, earning the title Asshiddiq (The Truthful Witness).

  • Freeing the Oppressed: Using his vast wealth, he purchased and liberated tortured Muslim slaves in Mecca, including Bilal bin Rabah and Amir bin Fuhayrah.

2. Companion of the Cave & The Hijrah

  • Thani Ithnayn: Handpicked by the Prophet ﷺ to be his sole companion on the perilous migration (Hijrah) to Medina, sheltered in Cave Thawr where the Quran immortalized his devotion: "When they were in the cave, he said to his companion: Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us" (At-Tawbah: 40).

3. The First Rightly-Guided Caliph (632–634 CE)

  • Steadfastness at the Prophet's Passing: Calmed the grief-stricken community with his legendary address: "Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has passed; but whoever worships Allah, Allah is alive and never dies."

  • Unification & Riddah Wars: Dispatched Usama's expedition, defeated rebel apostates and false prophets, unified Arabia, and commissioned the landmark first compilation of the Holy Quran into a single codex (Mushaf).

Passing & Historical Legacy

Abu Bakar passed away in Medina in 634 CE (13 AH) and was laid to rest beside the Holy Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the Prophet's Chamber. He is venerated as the greatest human being after the Prophets and Messengers.

Amr bin Luhay al-Khuza'i.role: Chief of Banu Khuza'ah & Introducer of Idolatry in Mecca
Amr bin Luhay al-Khuza'i.facts:
Full Name : Amr ibn Luhay ibn Qama'ah al-Khuza'i
Tribe : Banu Khuza'ah
Region : Mecca and al-Balqa (Levant)
Era / Setting : Pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah
Event : Introduction of Hubal & Alteration of Pilgrimage Rites
Amr bin Luhay al-Khuza'i.body:
Lineage & Early Life

Amr ibn Luhay ibn Qama'ah al-Khuza'i served as the foremost leader of Banu Khuza'ah after his tribe displaced Banu Jurhum from the stewardship of Mecca and the Ka'bah. As recorded by Ibn Hisham in Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, his generosity in provisioning pilgrims and administering communal affairs gave his decisions unquestioned religious authority across the Hijaz.

Key Events & Historical Role

1. Journey to al-Balqa and the Introduction of Hubal

  • Expedition to the Levant: Traveling to al-Balqa in southern Syria for trade and medical recovery, Amr observed local clans worshiping carved stone idols to invoke rain and military victory.

  • Installation at the Ka'bah: Persuaded by that custom, Amr brought back the red carnelian idol Hubal, set it beside the Ka'bah sanctuary, and urged Meccan tribes to venerate it.

2. Alteration of Abrahamic Rites

  • Consecrated Camel Offerings: Classical historians document that Amr instituted pre-Islamic pagan dedications such as sa'ibah and bahirah camels alongside coastal idol shrines like Manat, Lat, and Uzza.

  • Prophetic Testimony: Recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (nos. 3521 and 4623), Amr ibn Luhay is explicitly identified as the first individual to alter the monotheistic way of Ibrahim and establish the sa'ibah dedication in Arabia.

Death & Historical Legacy

His lineage retained custody of Mecca until Qusay ibn Kilab later unified the Quraysh clans in the 5th century CE. The hundreds of idols rooted during Amr's era remained around the Ka'bah until their complete removal during the Conquest of Mecca in 8 AH (630 CE).

About This Telling

Compiled directly from authenticated narrations on Sunnah.com (Sahih al-Bukhari 3521, 4623), Sirah Ibn Hisham, Tarikh al-Tabari, and Qur'an 5:103.

Era / Setting : Pre-Prophetic Era (Hanif)
Died : c. 605 CE (prior to the First Revelation)
Zaid bin Amr bin Nufail.body:
Lineage & Early Life

Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufail belonged to Banu Adi of Quraysh, making him uncle to Umar ibn al-Khattab and father to Sa'id ibn Zaid, one of the ten companions promised Paradise. Long before the call to prophethood, Zaid grew disillusioned with the polytheism engulfing Mecca and joined a small circle of seekers who resolved to recover the pure monotheism of Abraham.

Key Events & Historical Role

1. Public Rejection of Idols & Female Infanticide

  • Standing by the Ka'bah: As preserved in Sahih al-Bukhari (nos. 3826–3827), Zaid stood beside the Ka'bah declaring to the Quraysh that none among them remained upon the religion of Abraham except himself, refusing any meat slaughtered for idols.

  • Rescuing Daughters: He actively rescued infant girls threatened with live burial in pre-Islamic Mecca, raising them at his own expense until adulthood.

2. Travels Across Syria and Iraq

  • Seeking True Scripture: Zaid journeyed through Mosul and Greater Syria consulting Jewish scholars and Christian monks until a monk in Syria informed him that a prophet reviving the religion of Abraham was soon to arise in his own homeland of Mecca.

  • Exile at Mount Hira: Ostracized by his kinsman al-Khattab, Zaid often resided along the slopes of Hira outside Mecca while praying facing the Ka'bah.

Death & Historical Legacy

Returning toward Mecca upon hearing news of an imminent messenger around 605 CE, Zaid was slain by highwaymen near Lakhm five years before the first revelation. Islamic biographical sources preserve the Prophet's testimony that Zaid will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment as a single nation unto himself.

About This Telling

Synthesized from Sahih al-Bukhari (3826, 3827) via Sunnah.com, Siyar A'lam an-Nubala', and Sirah Ibn Hisham.
